chunks: Abu Dawood, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Does it suffice for me if I recite in the obligatory prayer only the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha) when I am in a hurry or something hastens me?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite only Surah Al-Fatiha in obligatory prayer if one is in a hurry?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of reciting only Surah Al-Fatiha in the obligatory prayer when pressed by time or necessity, highlighting the principle of ease (rukhas) in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the foundational status of Al-Fatiha as the essence of the Quran in prayer, allowing for flexibility without invalidating the act of worship. The response 'La ba'sa' (no harm) indicates a concession rather than a strict requirement, reflecting the practical adaptability of ritual law.

en.hubeali: Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Hasan Al Sayqal who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Would it suffice from me if I were to recite during the Obligatory (Salāt), the Opening of the Book (Chapter 1) only when I was in haste or something was hastening me?’ So heasws said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Dawud has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from Hassan al-Sayqaf who has said the foiiowing:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Is it sufficient for me to read just al-Fatihah in an obligatory Salah (prayer) if I am in a hurry or something causes me to move quickly?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’It is not harmful.’”
